title: Subprocess Fork Indirection Bypasses In-Process Component Architecture
summary: Multiple critical subsystems, notably the MCP server bridge in pkg/mcp/cli_bridge.go and the scheduler convergence engine in pkg/scheduler/convergence_engine.go, execute core domain operations by shelling out to the bin/zqk CLI binary via os/exec (exec.CommandContext), capturing stdout strings, regex-scrubbing log lines, and re-deserializing JSON, rather than invoking in-process Go packages. This introduces extreme process fork latency, memory overhead, context cancellation failure modes, and test-suite fork-bomb vulnerabilities.
recommendation: Refactor pkg/mcp and pkg/scheduler to invoke domain operations directly via in-process Go application interfaces (e.g. cli.ExecuteInProcess or domain service layers). Encapsulate command execution behind pure in-memory dispatcher interfaces that do not require external process spawning or stdout string scraping.

title: Asymmetric Persistence Guarantees and Interface Contract Divergence in ObjectStorageProvider
summary: The primary storage contract (ObjectStorageProvider in pkg/storage/object_storage_interface.go) defines a monolithic 25-method interface implemented by both FileObjectStorage and GraphObjectStorage, but their behavioral guarantees completely diverge. FileObjectStorage incorporates a 4-tier storage hierarchy (CAS, draft plane, stream storage, and direct YAML) with listing index queues and WAL, none of which exist in GraphObjectStorage. Conversely, FileObjectStorage.Query explicitly rejects non-filter queries (query.Type != QueryTypeFilter) with an error, causing consumers like pkg/verification/engine.go (which issues QueryTypeCypher) to fail unconditionally against the file backend, violating the Liskov Substitution Principle.
recommendation: Segregate ObjectStorageProvider into distinct, focused interfaces per the Interface Segregation Principle (ISP): e.g. ObjectStore (basic CRUD), GraphTraversalStore (relational graph traversal), and QueryableStore. Ensure behavioral parity or explicit feature capability negotiation rather than throwing runtime errors on valid interface methods.
non_goals: Forcing file storage to implement a full Cypher query engine

title: Lock Instrumentation Over-Abstraction and Allocation Overhead via 150+ String Constant Registry
summary: In pkg/concurrency and pkg/storage/locknames, every mutex acquisition across storage and caching layers is wrapped in concurrency.RunInLockWithLogger, supported by a registry of 340+ lines defining over 150 lock name string constants (LockName*). title: JobLock stale lock cleanup unlinks lock file breaking flock mutual exclusion
summary: JobLock implements distributed mutual exclusion for scheduler jobs across processes using POSIX flock. In NewJobLockWithConfig, NewFileLock opens lockPath and caches the open file descriptor. In Acquire() and TryAcquire(), checkAndCleanStaleLock() evaluates info.ModTime(). If age exceeds StaleLockThreshold (default 1h), it removes lockPath from disk via fileutil.Remove(). When fileLock.LockWithTimeout() then executes, it acquires flock on an unlinked inode. Concurrently, a second process calling NewJobLock creates and locks a brand new inode at the recreated lockPath. Both processes concurrently hold exclusive locks on different inodes, completely defeating mutual exclusion and allowing overlapping execution of singleton tasks.
recommendation: Never unlink an flock lock file to break stale locks. Instead, use non-blocking flock acquisition (unix.LOCK_NB) to verify whether another live process holds the lock; if flock succeeds, the lock is definitively not held regardless of file modification timestamp. If PID tracking is needed, record the owner PID in the file payload and check /proc or kill(pid, 0) before acquisition without unlinking the file.

title: Asynchronous tests substitute test assertions with t.Log, masking queue and retry failures
summary: In asynchronous subsystem tests (e.g. cmd/zqk/system/async_check_test.go), verification logic after asynchronous operations does not fail the test upon observing invalid states. In TestAsyncValidation_RetryExhaustion and TestAsyncValidation_ProgressReporting, conditions where queueSize > 0 or !errorReceived.Load() are logged via t.Log and t.Logf rather than asserted with t.Error or t.Fatal. If retries stall or progress reporting fails completely, the test reports PASS, defeating the purpose of the test.
recommendation: Upgrade all speculative t.Log and t.Logf messages in test verification blocks to strict t.Errorf or t.Fatalf assertions, ensuring asynchronous invariants are strictly enforced.
non_goals: Prohibiting informative logging in tests when accompanied by strict assertions
Eliminating asynchronous validator queue test coverage

evidence.detail: Test logs message instead of failing when queue still has tasks: if queueSize > 0 { t.Logf(...) }
Test logs note instead of failing when error progress is not received or tasks remain in queue

citations.point: Testing on the Toilet: Assert What You Care About. Logging a failure without calling t.Error or t.Fatal turns a test into dead documentation that never catches regressions.
Automated Testing Invariants: Tests must produce binary pass/fail results based on invariant assertions.

verification_proof: Remediated in codebase and verified under unit/race tests

title: Tests invoke unsynchronized os.Setenv without t.Setenv during parallel test execution
summary: While the vast majority of test packages have transitioned to t.Setenv (750 occurrences), 26 instances of unsynchronized os.Setenv remain in test files (e.g. pkg/testservices/services_extended_test.go:205, pkg/specialization/specialization_test.go:28, and pkg/zqkenv/env_alias_test.go:24). Unlike t.Setenv, os.Setenv directly mutates process-wide environment variables without Go test runner synchronization or automated cleanup, risking data races and test cross-talk when packages run concurrently.
recommendation: Replace all 26 instances of os.Setenv in *_test.go files with t.Setenv(key, val), ensuring automated test cleanup and panic prevention under parallel execution.
non_goals: Modifying TestMain functions where testing.T is unavailable and process-wide setup is deliberate

citations.point: testing.T.Setenv: Uses Cleanup to restore the environment variable to its original value after the test. Panics if called in a parallel test to prevent data races.

title: Strong hermetic filesystem isolation via t.TempDir across 2,674 test fixtures
summary: The test codebase demonstrates exemplary filesystem hermeticity: 2,674 test functions strictly employ t.TempDir() and automated cleanup routines (t.Cleanup), ensuring that multi-agent storage workspaces, CAS caches, and WAL repositories execute in isolated transient directories without polluting the host environment, user directories, or developer working trees.
recommendation: Maintain strict enforcement of t.TempDir() across all newly added storage, daemon, and CLI test fixtures.
non_goals: Modifying existing hermetic test harness patterns
